name: LitQA2
intro: LitQA2 是 FutureHouse 为检验跨科学文献检索与推理能力人工构建的 248 道英文多项选择题。作者与签约专家从过去 36 个月论文中选择必须依赖正文、不能仅凭标题或摘要回答且需要推理的发现，配制可信干扰项，并通过周期性模型挑战、Google Scholar 检索、新作者校准和持续审核决定接收、返工或剔除；只有接收题合入题库，返工题返回挑战测试。论文 v2 的 PaperQA 测量每次打乱选项，以温度 0 完整运行三次，用 GPT-4-0613 抽取字母答案，并报告准确率、已作答精确率与正确来源 DOI 归因召回率。论文规模为 248 题；固定 Hugging Face LAB-Bench 发布只有一个含 199 行的 train split，paper-qa 复现清单再从中选择 159 个 train ID 和 40 个 eval ID，另有 49 个来自自动门控语料的 test ID。
build_method: 作者与签约专家人工出题，周期性模型挑战与 Google Scholar 检索，新作者最初约10题校准及持续作者审核
metric: 准确率；已作答精确率；正确来源 DOI 归因召回率
task_type: 科学文献检索, 多项选择问答
eval_feature: 论文v2每次调用随机排列选项，信息不足/空标答规则，三次温度0完整运行，GPT-4-0613字母抽取，DOI归因
scale: 论文248题（47+100+101）；固定HF公开语料仅train=199行，paper-qa清单从中选train159+eval40；另有gated test49
build_method_en: Manual authoring by paper authors and contracted experts, periodic model challenges and Google Scholar searches, close calibration of roughly the first ten items from new authors, and continuing author review
eval_feature_en: Paper-v2 per-call choice randomization, insufficient-information/null-ideal grading, three full temperature-zero runs, GPT-4-0613 letter extraction, and DOI attribution
intro_en: LitQA2 is a 248-question English multiple-choice benchmark manually built by FutureHouse to test retrieval and reasoning across scientific literature. Authors and contracted experts select findings from papers published within the previous 36 months that require main-body context and reasoning rather than the title or abstract, add plausible distractors, and use periodic model challenges, Google Scholar searches, new-author calibration, and continuing review to accept, rework, or remove drafts. Only accepted items enter the corpus; reworked items return to challenge testing. The paper-v2 PaperQA measurement shuffles choices for every call, runs the full set three times at temperature zero, uses GPT-4-0613 to extract the answer letter, and reports accuracy, answered-question precision, and correct-source DOI attribution recall. The paper benchmark contains 248 questions. The pinned Hugging Face LAB-Bench release has one physical train split with 199 rows; the paper-qa reproduction manifest secondarily selects 159 train IDs and 40 eval IDs from those rows, plus 49 test IDs from an auto-gated corpus.
scale_en: Paper: 248 questions (47+100+101); pinned public HF corpus has only train=199 rows, from which the paper-qa manifest selects train159+eval40; gated test49 is separate
metric_en: Accuracy; answered-question precision; correct-source DOI attribution recall

drawio_review_note: Paper-alignment review passed on 2026-07-21 against arXiv:2409.13740v2 (revised 2024-09-26), the original PDF Methods 8.2, current paper-qa commit d7675d7b7eddeb3535e8c260399c5bbeeb818c50, LAB-Bench commit 998a8e0a40cf116c80e1b0e7a805ebb5fb9fa838, public Hugging Face revision 5c77cec648430f30611808808861eb86f81d5eaa, auto-gated aviary-paper-data revision e9ee5486ac60f06f9e7f217ca167e2a83874ded4, and Aviary commit 1c061dbc37febccf9f94d8e8308a0ddebb5dae3c. LitQA2 questions were manually generated by the paper authors and contracted experts. Authors selected papers published within the previous 36 months, required main-body context and reasoning rather than titles, abstracts, or direct quotations, recorded the intended source DOI, and constructed plausible distractors from other paper facts or domain knowledge. Some items were intentionally unanswerable. Drafts were periodically tested with ChatGPT 3.5 or 4 with logging disabled, often searched in Google Scholar, and excluded or revised when a model or human could answer from an alternative source. One or more paper authors closely reviewed roughly the first ten items from a new or contracted author, followed by ongoing author review. This is a real decision gate: accepted items merge into the corpus, reworked items return to challenge testing, and removed items terminate outside the corpus. The benchmark grew from the original 47 LitQA questions by 100 and then by a later unseen 101, reaching 248. For the reported PaperQA measurement, answer order was randomized for every call, one paperqa call was made per question, and every shown configuration used three complete runs at temperature zero. GPT-4-0613 received the exact extraction text 'Extract the single letter answer from the following question and answer {prompt_output(‘QA’)}' followed by 'Single Letter Answer:'. The parsed letter was graded against the ideal: selecting insufficient information was Unsure, except that it was Correct when the ideal was null. Accuracy is correct divided by all questions; precision is correct divided by answered questions; DOI recall is the percentage of all questions whose answer was attributed to the recorded correct source DOI. The pinned public Hugging Face LitQA2 configuration has one physical train split containing 199 rows and no physical eval or test split. The paper-qa reproduction manifest imposes a secondary ID partition over that corpus, selecting 159 train IDs and 40 eval IDs; its 49 test IDs instead come from the auto-gated aviary-paper-data corpus. This manifest-level 159/40/49 partition must not be conflated with either physical Hugging Face splits or the paper's old-147/new-101 development chronology. Both dataset cards declare CC BY-SA 4.0; the test repository requires an automatic contact-sharing gate, so LitQA2 is partly public, and no official live leaderboard or submission service was found. Exact source-paper sampling frame, candidate count, ChatGPT challenge prompts and generation settings, acceptance rate, reviewer agreement, and full revision/rejection logs are not published. Current software defaults also drift from the paper protocol: paper-qa retains a different extraction-prompt constant, while current Aviary defaults to gpt-4o-mini and verbatim option-text extraction, and only shuffles answer choices when a shuffle seed is explicitly supplied. Those current defaults are documented as drift and are not used to reconstruct the paper-v2 results.
